reason: I browse in Explorer and double-click whatever opens, so I don't have a viewer to replace, and nothing I open every week is failing right now. It's free so I'd try it once on a weird file, but I wouldn't go through Settings to make it my default.
why_switch_or_not: The speed pitch doesn't move me, because 40 ms vs 600 ms on rapid next is not something I do with relatives' photos. The only thing that could pull me in is a file type that currently fails for me, like a WebP or AVIF someone sends, but HEIC needs the Microsoft extension anyway so it doesn't help there. I'd also have to tick formats and press Set default myself, and a one-person 0.4.1 app with an English-only interface doesn't earn that effort.
current_app_pros: Explorer thumbnails let me see what's in a folder at a glance without opening anything, and whatever app opens the file is good enough for a photo. There's nothing to install or learn.
current_app_pains: Nothing much. Occasionally a file doesn't open or I have to pick an app, and printing a photo takes a few clicks. That's minor.
objection: The speed difference is a few tens of milliseconds, I would not feel it, and nothing in the description says it makes printing a relative's photo any easier.
would_change_my_mind: If it opened a photo type from my relatives that currently fails or shows a blank in Explorer or my default app, and printing was one obvious click, I'd keep it.
